- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias by 5–10% relative to recent mean.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots — cap forecast peak at 1.5x prior high or 10% below recent 10-day moving average.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0 to +0.3), model tends to overestimate — apply 3–5% downward adjustment to forecast mean.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon — shift forecast baseline 2–4% higher relative to 10-day moving average.  
- When sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from -0.6 to +0.3 in 3–5 days), model lags — adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift within 2–3 days, not 7–10.  
- Avoid forecasting below 65% of recent 18-day low — if sentiment is negative, cap forecast at 65% of prior 18-day low to prevent extreme underestimation.
